passages.text: As the time drew near for David to die, he charged his son Solomon, “I am about to go the way of all the earth. So be strong and prove yourself a man.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David was old and near death.
David called his son Solomon.
David spoke to Solomon.
David said, “I am about to die.
Everyone on earth must die.
Be strong.
Show that you are a man.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרְב֥וּ יְמֵֽי־ דָוִ֖ד לָמ֑וּת וַיְצַ֛ו אֶת־ שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃ אָנֹכִ֣י הֹלֵ֔ךְ בְּדֶ֖רֶךְ כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְחָזַקְתָּ֖ וְהָיִ֥יתָֽ לְאִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: And keep the charge of the LORD your God to walk in His ways and to keep His statutes, commandments, ordinances, and decrees, as is written in the Law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all you do and wherever you turn, and so that the LORD may fulfill His promise to me: ‘If your descendants take heed to walk faithfully before Me with all their heart and soul, you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.’
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to his son Solomon.
David told Solomon to obey the LORD God.
David told Solomon to follow the LORD’s ways.
David told Solomon to keep the LORD’s statutes.
David told Solomon to keep the LORD’s commandments.
David told Solomon to keep the LORD’s ordinances.
David told Solomon to keep the LORD’s decrees.
These commands are written in the Law of Moses.
If Solomon obeys, he will have wisdom in everything he does.
If Solomon obeys, he will have success wherever he goes.
If Solomon obeys, the LORD will keep His promise to David.
The LORD promised David that if his descendants walk faithfully before Him,
If they do this with all their heart and with all their soul,
Then David will always have a descendant on the throne of Israel.
passages.original: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֞ אֶת־ מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ לָלֶ֤כֶת בִּדְרָכָיו֙ לִשְׁמֹ֨ר חֻקֹּתָ֤יו מִצְוֺתָיו֙ וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֣יו וְעֵדְוֺתָ֔יו כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּתוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֑ה לְמַ֣עַן תַּשְׂכִּ֗יל אֵ֚ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּפְנֶ֖ה שָֽׁם׃ לְמַעַן֩ יָקִ֨ים יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלַי֮ לֵאמֹר֒ אִם־ יִשְׁמְר֨וּ בָנֶ֜יךָ אֶת־ דַּרְכָּ֗ם לָלֶ֤כֶת לְפָנַי֙ בֶּאֱמֶ֔ת בְּכָל־ לְבָבָ֖ם וּבְכָל־ נַפְשָׁ֑ם לֵאמֹ֕ר לֹֽא־ יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Moreover, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me—what he did to Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of the armies of Israel. He killed them in peacetime to avenge the blood of war. He stained with the blood of war the belt around his waist and the sandals on his feet.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the son of Zeruiah.
You know what Joab did to me.
You know what Joab did to Abner son of Ner.
You know what Joab did to Amasa son of Jether.
Abner and Amasa were commanders of the armies of Israel.
Joab killed Abner and Amasa.
Joab killed them during a time of peace.
Joab killed them as if it were a time of war.
Joab put the blood of war on his belt around his waist.
Joab put the blood of war on the sandals on his feet.
passages.original: וְגַ֣ם אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֡עְתָּ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁר־ עָ֨שָׂה לִ֜י יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־ צְרוּיָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֣ה לִשְׁנֵֽי־ שָׂרֵ֣י צִבְא֣וֹת יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל לְאַבְנֵ֨ר בֶּן־ נֵ֜ר וְלַעֲמָשָׂ֤א בֶן־ יֶ֙תֶר֙ וַיַּ֣הַרְגֵ֔ם וַיָּ֥שֶׂם דְּמֵֽי־ מִלְחָמָ֖ה בְּשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיִּתֵּ֞ן דְּמֵ֣י מִלְחָמָ֗ה בַּחֲגֹֽרָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמָתְנָ֔יו וּֽבְנַעֲל֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרַגְלָֽיו׃

passages.text: So act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.
passages.sermon: You must act with wisdom.\r\nYou must not let Joab die peacefully in old age.\r\nYou must not allow his gray hair to go down to the grave in peace.
passages.original: וְעָשִׂ֖יתָ כְּחָכְמָתֶ֑ךָ וְלֹֽא־ תוֹרֵ֧ד שֵׂיבָת֛וֹ בְּשָׁלֹ֖ם שְׁאֹֽל׃ס

passages.text: But show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, because they stood by me when I fled from your brother Absalom.
passages.sermon:
Barzillai was a Gileadite.
He had sons.
Show kindness to the sons of Barzillai.
Let them eat at your table.
They helped me.
I fled from your brother Absalom.
They stood by me during that time.
passages.original: וְלִבְנֵ֨י בַרְזִלַּ֤י הַגִּלְעָדִי֙ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־ חֶ֔סֶד וְהָי֖וּ בְּאֹכְלֵ֣י שֻׁלְחָנֶ֑ךָ כִּי־ כֵן֙ קָרְב֣וּ אֵלַ֔י בְּבָרְחִ֕י מִפְּנֵ֖י אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם אָחִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Keep an eye on Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim who is with you. He called down bitter curses against me on the day I went to Mahanaim, but when he came down to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by the LORD: ‘I will never put you to the sword.’
passages.sermon:
Shimei is with you now.
Shimei is the son of Gera.
Shimei is a Benjamite from Bahurim.
Shimei cursed me with bitter curses.
He cursed me on the day I went to Mahanaim.
Later, Shimei came down to meet me at the Jordan River.
I swore to Shimei by the LORD.
I said, “I will not put you to death by the sword.”
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֣ה עִ֠מְּךָ שִֽׁמְעִ֨י בֶן־ גֵּרָ֥א בֶן־ הַיְמִינִי֮ מִבַּחֻרִים֒ וְה֤וּא קִֽלְלַ֙נִי֙ קְלָלָ֣ה נִמְרֶ֔צֶת בְּי֖וֹם לֶכְתִּ֣י מַחֲנָ֑יִם וְהֽוּא־ יָרַ֤ד לִקְרָאתִי֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וָאֶשָּׁ֨בַֽע ל֤וֹ בַֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אִם־ אֲמִֽיתְךָ֖ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: Now therefore, do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man. You know what you ought to do to him to bring his gray head down to Sheol in blood.”
passages.sermon:
Solomon, you are a wise man.
Do not let Shimei go unpunished.
You know what you should do to him.
Make sure he dies a violent death and goes down to the grave with blood.
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ אַל־ תְּנַקֵּ֔הוּ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ חָכָ֖ם אָ֑תָּה וְיָֽדַעְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־ לּ֔וֹ וְהוֹרַדְתָּ֧ אֶת־ שֵׂיבָת֛וֹ בְּדָ֖ם שְׁאֽוֹל׃

passages.text: Then David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.
passages.sermon: David was the king of Israel.\r\nDavid died.\r\nPeople buried David in the City of David.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב דָּוִ֖ד עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּעִ֥יר דָּוִֽד׃פ

passages.text: The length of David’s reign over Israel was forty years—seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
David was king over Israel.
He ruled for forty years.
He ruled in Hebron for seven years.
He ruled in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.
passages.original: וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָלַ֤ךְ דָּוִד֙ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּחֶבְר֤וֹן מָלַךְ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם מָלַ֔ךְ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֹ֖שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly established.
passages.sermon:
Solomon became king after his father David died.
Solomon sat on David’s throne.
Solomon ruled as king.
His kingdom became very strong.
His rule was firmly established.
passages.original: וּשְׁלֹמֹ֕ה יָשַׁ֕ב עַל־ כִּסֵּ֖א דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַתִּכֹּ֥ן מַלְכֻת֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Now Adonijah son of Haggith went to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, and she asked, “Do you come in peace?” “Yes, in peace,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Adonijah was the son of Haggith.
Bathsheba was the mother of Solomon.
Adonijah went to Bathsheba.
Bathsheba asked Adonijah a question.
She said, “Do you come in peace?”
Adonijah answered her.
He said, “Yes, in peace.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֞א אֲדֹנִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־ חַגֵּ֗ית אֶל־ בַּת־ שֶׁ֙בַע֙ אֵם־ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתֹּ֖אמֶר הֲשָׁל֣וֹם בֹּאֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Then he said, “I have something to tell you.” “Say it,” she answered.
passages.sermon:
Adonijah spoke to Bathsheba.
He said, "I have something to tell you."
Bathsheba answered him.
She said, "Say it."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דָּבָ֥ר לִ֖י אֵלָ֑יִךְ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: “You know that the kingship was mine,” he said. “All Israel expected that I should reign, but the kingship has turned to my brother, for it has come to him from the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Adonijah was the son of Haggith.
Bathsheba was the mother of Solomon.
Adonijah spoke to Bathsheba.
Adonijah said, “You know the kingship belonged to me.
All Israel looked to me to be king.
The kingship turned away from me.
Now my brother has the kingship.
The LORD gave the kingship to my brother.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַ֤תְּ יָדַ֙עַתְּ֙ כִּי־ לִי֙ הָיְתָ֣ה הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה וְעָלַ֞י שָׂ֧מוּ כָֽל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם לִמְלֹ֑ךְ וַתִּסֹּ֤ב הַמְּלוּכָה֙ וַתְּהִ֣י לְאָחִ֔י כִּ֥י מֵיְהוָ֖ה הָ֥יְתָה לּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So now I have just one request of you; do not deny me.” “State your request,” she told him.
passages.sermon:
Adonijah spoke to Bathsheba.
He said, “Now I have one request from you.
Do not refuse me.”
Bathsheba answered him.
She said, “Speak.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁאֵלָ֤ה אַחַת֙ אָֽנֹכִי֙ שֹׁאֵ֣ל מֵֽאִתָּ֔ךְ אַל־ תָּשִׁ֖בִי אֶת־ פָּנָ֑י וַתֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו דַּבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: Adonijah replied, “Please speak to King Solomon, since he will not turn you down. Let him give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife.”
passages.sermon:
Adonijah spoke to Bathsheba.
Adonijah was Solomon’s older brother.
Adonijah wanted something from King Solomon.
Adonijah said, “Please speak to King Solomon for me.”
Adonijah believed Solomon would listen to Bathsheba.
Adonijah said, “He will not refuse you.”
Adonijah asked for Abishag the Shunammite.
Adonijah wanted Abishag as his wife.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִמְרִי־ נָא֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֥י לֹֽא־ יָשִׁ֖יב אֶת־ פָּנָ֑יִךְ וְיִתֶּן־ לִ֛י אֶת־ אֲבִישַׁ֥ג הַשּׁוּנַמִּ֖ית לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: “Very well,” Bathsheba replied. “I will speak to the king for you.”
passages.sermon:
Bathsheba was Solomon’s mother.
Adonijah asked Bathsheba for help.
Bathsheba answered Adonijah.
She said, “Very well.”
She said, “I will speak to the king for you.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר בַּת־ שֶׁ֖בַע ט֑וֹב אָנֹכִ֕י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ אֶל־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king stood up to greet her, bowed to her, and sat down on his throne. Then the king had a throne brought for his mother, who sat down at his right hand.
passages.sermon:
Bathsheba was Solomon’s mother.
Bathsheba went to King Solomon.
She wanted to speak to him about Adonijah.
King Solomon stood up to greet Bathsheba.
King Solomon bowed to Bathsheba.
King Solomon sat down on his throne.
King Solomon brought a throne for his mother.
Bathsheba sat at the king’s right hand.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֤א בַת־ שֶׁ֙בַע֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לְדַבֶּר־ ל֖וֹ עַל־ אֲדֹנִיָּ֑הוּ וַיָּקָם֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ לִקְרָאתָ֜הּ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֣חוּ לָ֗הּ וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ עַל־ כִּסְא֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם כִּסֵּא֙ לְאֵ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתֵּ֖שֶׁב לִֽימִינֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “I have just one small request of you,” she said. “Do not deny me.” “Make your request, my mother,” the king replied, “for I will not deny you.”
passages.sermon:
Bathsheba was the mother of King Solomon.
Bathsheba spoke to King Solomon.
Bathsheba said, “I have one small request from you.”
Bathsheba said, “Do not refuse me.”
King Solomon answered his mother.
King Solomon said, “Ask, my mother.”
King Solomon said, “I will not refuse you.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שְׁאֵלָ֨ה אַחַ֤ת קְטַנָּה֙ אָֽנֹכִי֙ שֹׁאֶ֣לֶת מֵֽאִתָּ֔ךְ אַל־ תָּ֖שֶׁב אֶת־ פָּנָ֑י וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ לָ֤הּ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ שַׁאֲלִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֥י לֹֽא־ אָשִׁ֖יב אֶת־ פָּנָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: So Bathsheba said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife.”
passages.sermon:
Bathsheba was the mother of King Solomon.
She spoke to King Solomon.
Bathsheba made a request to Solomon.
She said, “Give Abishag the Shunammite to your brother Adonijah as a wife.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר יֻתַּ֖ן אֶת־ אֲבִישַׁ֣ג הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֑ית לַאֲדֹנִיָּ֥הוּ אָחִ֖יךָ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: King Solomon answered his mother, “Why do you request Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Since he is my older brother, you might as well request the kingdom for him and for Abiathar the priest and for Joab son of Zeruiah!”
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the son of David and Bathsheba.
King Solomon was the king of Israel.
Bathsheba was Solomon’s mother.
King Solomon spoke to his mother.
He said, “Why do you ask for Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah?”
Adonijah was Solomon’s older brother.
Solomon said, “You might as well ask for the kingdom for Adonijah.”
He said, “Adonijah is my older brother.”
He said, “You might as well ask for the kingdom for Abiathar the priest.”
He said, “You might as well ask for the kingdom for Joab son of Zeruiah.”
passages.original: וַיַּעַן֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאִמּ֗וֹ וְלָמָה֩ אַ֨תְּ שֹׁאֶ֜לֶת אֶת־ אֲבִישַׁ֤ג הַשֻּׁנַמִּית֙ לַאֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ וְשַֽׁאֲלִי־ לוֹ֙ אֶת־ הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה כִּ֛י ה֥וּא אָחִ֖י הַגָּד֣וֹל מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְלוֹ֙ וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וּלְיוֹאָ֖ב בֶּן־ צְרוּיָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD: “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if Adonijah has not made this request at the expense of his life.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the son of David and the king of Israel.
King Solomon spoke with authority.
King Solomon swore an oath by the LORD.
King Solomon said, “May God punish me if I am not truthful.
May God punish me even more if I am wrong.
Adonijah has spoken this request against his own life.
Adonijah has endangered his own life by making this request.”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׁבַע֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה בַּֽיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֣ה יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֔יף כִּ֣י בְנַפְשׁ֔וֹ דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And now, as surely as the LORD lives—the One who established me, who set me on the throne of my father David, and who founded for me a dynasty as He promised—surely Adonijah shall be put to death today!”
passages.sermon:
King Solomon spoke.
The LORD lives.
The LORD established me as king.
The LORD set me on the throne of my father David.
The LORD made a house for me, just as He promised.
Today, Adonijah will die.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה חַי־ יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֱכִינַ֗נִי וַיּוֹשִׁיבִינִי עַל־ כִּסֵּא֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י וַאֲשֶׁ֧ר עָֽשָׂה־ לִ֛י בַּ֖יִת כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר כִּ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם יוּמַ֖ת אֲדֹנִיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: So King Solomon sent the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who struck down Adonijah, and he died.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon gave an order.
He gave the order to Benaiah.
Benaiah was the son of Jehoiada.
Benaiah went to Adonijah.
Benaiah struck Adonijah.
Adonijah died.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד בְּנָיָ֣הוּ בֶן־ יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע וַיִּפְגַּע־ בּ֖וֹ וַיָּמֹֽת׃ס

passages.text: Then the king said to Abiathar the priest, “Go back to your fields in Anathoth. Even though you deserve to die, I will not put you to death at this time, since you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and you suffered through all that my father suffered.”
passages.sermon:
King Solomon spoke to Abiathar the priest.
He said, “Go to your fields in Anathoth.
You deserve to die.
But I will not put you to death today.
You carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David.
You suffered in everything my father suffered.”
passages.original: וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֨ר הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֲנָתֹת֙ לֵ֣ךְ עַל־ שָׂדֶ֔יךָ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ מָ֖וֶת אָ֑תָּה וּבַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה לֹ֣א אֲמִיתֶ֗ךָ כִּֽי־ נָשָׂ֜אתָ אֶת־ אֲר֨וֹן אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהֹוִה֙ לִפְנֵי֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י וְכִ֣י הִתְעַנִּ֔יתָ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־ הִתְעַנָּ֖ה אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: So Solomon banished Abiathar from the priesthood of the LORD and thus fulfilled the word that the LORD had spoken at Shiloh against the house of Eli.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon removed Abiathar from being a priest to the LORD.
Solomon did this to fulfill the word of the LORD.
The LORD had spoken this word at Shiloh.
The LORD spoke against the house of Eli.
passages.original: וַיְגָ֤רֶשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֶת־ אֶבְיָתָ֔ר מִהְי֥וֹת כֹּהֵ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה לְמַלֵּא֙ אֶת־ דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֛ר עַל־ בֵּ֥ית עֵלִ֖י בְּשִׁלֹֽה׃פ

passages.text: When the news reached Joab, who had conspired with Adonijah but not with Absalom, he fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
passages.sermon:
Joab was a military leader under King David.
Joab supported Adonijah in his attempt to become king.
Joab did not support Absalom.
Joab heard news about recent events.
Joab fled to the tent of the LORD.
Joab grabbed the horns of the altar inside the tent.
passages.original: וְהַשְּׁמֻעָה֙ בָּ֣אָה עַד־ יוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֣י יוֹאָ֗ב נָטָה֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֲדֹנִיָּ֔ה וְאַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם לֹ֣א נָטָ֑ה וַיָּ֤נָס יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־ אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּקַרְנ֥וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: It was reported to King Solomon: “Joab has fled to the tent of the LORD and is now beside the altar.” So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, strike him down!”
passages.sermon:
King Solomon received a report.
The report said, “Joab has fled to the tent of the LORD.”
Joab is now beside the altar.
Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada.
Solomon said, “Go, strike him down.”
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֞ד לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כִּ֣י נָ֤ס יוֹאָב֙ אֶל־ אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה אֵ֣צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת־ בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־ יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע לֵאמֹ֖ר לֵ֥ךְ פְּגַע־ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And Benaiah entered the tent of the LORD and said to Joab, “The king says, ‘Come out!’ ” But Joab replied, “No, I will die here.” So Benaiah relayed the message to the king, saying, “This is how Joab answered me.”
passages.sermon:
Benaiah was a commander under King Solomon.
Joab was a former commander who had supported Adonijah against Solomon.
Joab fled to the tent of the LORD for safety.
Benaiah entered the tent of the LORD.
Benaiah spoke to Joab.
Benaiah said, “The king says, ‘Come out!’”
Joab answered Benaiah.
Joab said, “No, I will die here.”
Benaiah returned to King Solomon.
Benaiah told the king what Joab had said.
Benaiah said, “This is how Joab answered me.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א בְנָיָ֜הוּ אֶל־ אֹ֣הֶל יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ צֵ֔א וַיֹּ֥אמֶר׀ לֹ֖א כִּ֣י פֹ֣ה אָמ֑וּת וַיָּ֨שֶׁב בְּנָיָ֤הוּ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ דָּבָ֣ר לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּֽה־ דִבֶּ֥ר יוֹאָ֖ב וְכֹ֥ה עָנָֽנִי׃

passages.text: And the king replied, “Do just as he says. Strike him down and bury him, and so remove from me and from the house of my father the innocent blood that Joab shed.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon spoke to Benaiah son of Jehoiada.
King Solomon said, "Do as Joab has said."
"Strike Joab down."
"Bury him."
"By doing this, you will remove innocent blood."
"Joab shed this innocent blood."
"You will take away this guilt from me."
"You will also take away this guilt from my father's house."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֲשֵׂה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר וּפְגַע־ בּ֖וֹ וּקְבַרְתּ֑וֹ וַהֲסִירֹ֣תָ׀ דְּמֵ֣י חִנָּ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁפַ֣ךְ יוֹאָ֔ב מֵעָלַ֕י וּמֵעַ֖ל בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: The LORD will bring his bloodshed back upon his own head, for without the knowledge of my father David he struck down two men more righteous and better than he when he put to the sword Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah’s army.
passages.sermon:
The LORD will return Joab’s bloodshed onto Joab’s own head.
Joab killed two men.
These two men were more righteous and better than Joab.
Joab killed them with the sword.
My father David did not know about these killings.
Joab killed Abner son of Ner.
Abner was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab also killed Amasa son of Jether.
Amasa was the commander of Judah’s army.
passages.original: וְהֵשִׁיב֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת־ דָּמ֜וֹ עַל־ רֹאשׁ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּגַ֣ע בִּשְׁנֵֽי־ אֲ֠נָשִׁים צַדִּקִ֨ים וְטֹבִ֤ים מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ וַיַּהַרְגֵ֣ם בַּחֶ֔רֶב וְאָבִ֥י דָוִ֖ד לֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע אֶת־ אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן־ נֵר֙ שַׂר־ צְבָ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־ עֲמָשָׂ֥א בֶן־ יֶ֖תֶר שַׂר־ צְבָ֥א יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Their blood will come back upon the heads of Joab and his descendants forever; but for David, his descendants, his house, and his throne, there shall be peace from the LORD forever.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in Israel.
Joab killed innocent men.
God will punish Joab for this.
The guilt for their blood will stay on Joab.
The guilt will also stay on Joab’s descendants forever.
David was king of Israel.
God will give peace to David.
God will give peace to David’s descendants.
God will give peace to David’s house.
God will give peace to David’s throne.
This peace from the LORD will last forever.
passages.original: וְשָׁ֤בוּ דְמֵיהֶם֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹאָ֔ב וּבְרֹ֥אשׁ זַרְע֖וֹ לְעֹלָ֑ם וּלְדָוִ֡ד וּ֠לְזַרְעוֹ וּלְבֵית֨וֹ וּלְכִסְא֜וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה שָׁל֛וֹם עַד־ עוֹלָ֖ם מֵעִ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck down Joab, and killed him. He was buried at his own home in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
Benaiah was the son of Jehoiada.
Benaiah went up to Joab.
Benaiah struck Joab.
Benaiah killed Joab.
People buried Joab at his own home.
Joab’s home was in the wilderness.
passages.original: וַיַּ֗עַל בְּנָיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־ יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וַיִּפְגַּע־ בּ֖וֹ וַיְמִתֵ֑הוּ וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר בְּבֵית֖וֹ בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: And the king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada in Joab’s place over the army, and he appointed Zadok the priest in Abiathar’s place.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon made new leaders.
He put Benaiah son of Jehoiada in charge of the army.
Benaiah replaced Joab as commander.
King Solomon also chose Zadok to be priest.
Zadok replaced Abiathar as priest.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־ בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־ יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע תַּחְתָּ֖יו עַל־ הַצָּבָ֑א וְאֶת־ צָד֤וֹק הַכֹּהֵן֙ נָתַ֣ן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ תַּ֖חַת אֶבְיָתָֽר׃

passages.text: Then the king summoned Shimei and said to him, “Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem and live there, but do not go anywhere else.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon summoned Shimei.
Shimei was a man living in Israel.
King Solomon spoke to Shimei.
He said, “Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem.
Live in Jerusalem.
Do not leave Jerusalem.
Do not go anywhere else.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וַיִּקְרָ֣א לְשִׁמְעִ֔י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ בְּֽנֵה־ לְךָ֥ בַ֙יִת֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֖ שָׁ֑ם וְלֹֽא־ תֵצֵ֥א מִשָּׁ֖ם אָ֥נֶה וָאָֽנָה׃

passages.text: On the day you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, know for sure that you will die; your blood will be on your own head.”
passages.sermon:
King Solomon spoke to Shimei.
King Solomon gave Shimei a command.
King Solomon said, “Do not leave Jerusalem.
Do not cross the Kidron Valley.
If you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, you will die that day.
You will be responsible for your own death.
Your blood will be on your own head.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה׀ בְּי֣וֹם צֵאתְךָ֗ וְעָֽבַרְתָּ֙ אֶת־ נַ֣חַל קִדְר֔וֹן יָדֹ֥עַ תֵּדַ֖ע כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת דָּמְךָ֖ יִהְיֶ֥ה בְרֹאשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: “The sentence is fair,” Shimei replied. “Your servant will do as my lord the king has spoken.” And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.
passages.sermon:
Shimei spoke to the king.
Shimei said, "The command is good."
Shimei said, "I will do as my lord the king has said."
Shimei was a servant of the king.
Shimei lived in Jerusalem.
He stayed there for many days.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שִׁמְעִ֤י לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ ט֣וֹב הַדָּבָ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב שִׁמְעִ֛י בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃ס

passages.text: After three years, however, two of Shimei’s slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. And Shimei was told, “Look, your slaves are in Gath.”
passages.sermon:
Shimei was a man living in Jerusalem.
Three years passed.
Two slaves belonged to Shimei.
These two slaves ran away.
They went to Achish.
Achish was the son of Maacah.
Achish was the king of Gath.
Someone told Shimei about his slaves.
The person said, “Your slaves are in Gath.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וַיִּבְרְח֤וּ שְׁנֵֽי־ עֲבָדִים֙ לְשִׁמְעִ֔י אֶל־ אָכִ֥ישׁ בֶּֽן־ מַעֲכָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ גַּ֑ת וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לְשִׁמְעִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֥ה עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ בְּגַֽת׃

passages.text: So Shimei saddled his donkey and set out to Achish at Gath in search of his slaves, and he brought them back from Gath.
passages.sermon:
Shimei was a man living in Jerusalem.
Two of Shimei’s slaves ran away to Gath.
Gath was ruled by Achish, son of Maacah.
Shimei heard that his slaves were in Gath.
Shimei got up.
He saddled his donkey.
He traveled to Gath.
He went to Achish to find his slaves.
Shimei found his slaves in Gath.
He brought his slaves back from Gath.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם שִׁמְעִ֗י וַֽיַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ אֶת־ חֲמֹר֔וֹ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ גַּ֙תָה֙ אֶל־ אָכִ֔ישׁ לְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־ עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שִׁמְעִ֔י וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת־ עֲבָדָ֖יו מִגַּֽת׃

passages.text: When Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned, the king summoned Shimei and said to him, “Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, ‘On the day you leave and go elsewhere, know for sure that you will die’? And you told me, ‘The sentence is fair; I will comply.’
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
\r\nShimei was a man living in Jerusalem.
\r\nSomeone told Solomon that Shimei had left Jerusalem.
\r\nShimei went to Gath.
\r\nShimei returned to Jerusalem.
\r\nSolomon heard about Shimei’s journey.
\r\nSolomon sent for Shimei.
\r\nSolomon called Shimei to come to him.
\r\nSolomon spoke to Shimei.
\r\nSolomon said, “I made you swear by the LORD.”
\r\nSolomon said, “I warned you.”
\r\nSolomon said, “If you leave Jerusalem and go anywhere else, you will surely die.”
\r\nSolomon reminded Shimei, “You agreed to this.”
\r\nShimei had said, “This is a good command. I accept it.”
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה כִּי־ הָלַ֨ךְ שִׁמְעִ֧י מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם גַּ֖ת וַיָּשֹֽׁב׃ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַיִּקְרָ֣א לְשִׁמְעִ֗י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו הֲל֧וֹא הִשְׁבַּעְתִּ֣יךָ בַֽיהוָ֗ה וָאָעִ֤ד בְּךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּי֣וֹם צֵאתְךָ֗ וְהָֽלַכְתָּ֙ אָ֣נֶה וָאָ֔נָה יָדֹ֥עַ תֵּדַ֖ע כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת וַתֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלַ֛י ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָ֖ר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃

passages.text: So why have you not kept your oath to the LORD and the command that I gave you?”
passages.sermon:
King Solomon spoke to Shimei.
King Solomon asked Shimei a question.
King Solomon said, “You made an oath to the LORD.
You promised to obey the LORD.
I also gave you a command.
You did not keep your oath to the LORD.
You did not obey the command I gave you.
Why did you not keep your oath?
Why did you not obey my command?”
passages.original: וּמַדּ֕וּעַ לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔רְתָּ אֵ֖ת שְׁבֻעַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת־ הַמִּצְוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־ צִוִּ֥יתִי עָלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: The king also said, “You know in your heart all the evil that you did to my father David. Therefore the LORD will bring your evil back upon your head.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon spoke to Shimei.
Solomon was the son of David and the king of Israel.
Solomon said to Shimei, “You know what you have done.
You know all the evil you did to my father David.
Your own heart knows your actions.
The LORD will return your evil upon your own head.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־ שִׁמְעִ֗י אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֙עְתָּ֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־ הָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָדַע֙ לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָ לְדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י וְהֵשִׁ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ רָעָתְךָ֖ בְּרֹאשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: But King Solomon will be blessed and David’s throne will remain secure before the LORD forever.”
passages.sermon: King Solomon will be blessed.\r\nDavid’s throne will remain secure.\r\nThe throne will stand before the LORD forever.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בָּר֑וּךְ וְכִסֵּ֣א דָוִ֗ד יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֛וֹן לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. Thus the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solomon.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon gave an order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada.
Benaiah went out.
Benaiah struck Shimei.
Shimei died.
The kingdom became firmly established in Solomon’s hand.
passages.original: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶת־ בְּנָיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־ יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וַיֵּצֵ֕א וַיִּפְגַּע־ בּ֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהַמַּמְלָכָ֥ה נָכ֖וֹנָה בְּיַד־ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃
